2CNYns4imTBYe52m98xXqM: Nic Cester meant this as a Roll Over Beethoven for now: Chuck Berry's idea, with the composer swapped for whoever's on the decks. 3OYPskZPKnOcHZ9fUDwmCK: He'd been producing a record for Jessica Lea Mayfield, singing a lot of the harmonies up high, and he brought that voice home to his own band, where he'd never used it before. 5vefQfYc9Oxn8VHfgUCi1q: Before anybody had heard of them, Alex Turner worked behind the bar at the Boardwalk in Sheffield and watched a lot of bands. 5NIyDZfdnMGRXnwbX2kwA4: Jack Allsopp from London wrote this about the other end of fame: the flop stars, the kids who'll do anything to get on the telly, and the people in suits making money off the lot of them. 1LggghHQU8QOOC2AQ4WbWO: A band from Copenhagen, Mette Lindberg singing and Lars Iversen making the music with her. 0bKAmgLzk3LTHQgD5PFGej: George Kooymans and Barry Hay wrote this, and in nineteen eighty-four it was their fifth number one at home. 1MYlx4dBtiyjn7K8YSyfzT: The album was done. Then Jimmy Iovine, who ran the record company, said it still needed a song to open the door, the way My Name Is had the time before. 55USWnZ2JKfhvAzer2bxET: Ray Davies wrote this to follow You Really Got Me, out of the same stuff: a few fat chords and a brother with a temper on lead guitar. 57bgtoPSgt236HzfBOd8kj: The story the band liked to tell was about Angus Young on a plane that got hit by lightning. 278Ao6KQDxWGGszv24uvhI: Billie Joe Armstrong said this was the first song he wrote for the record, in their studio in Oakland, and that it's about two things he saw growing into each other: the mass shootings in America, and everybody filming everything to put online.
